_preregistration.supersedes: F167's K=64 measurement; copy_vs_repeat.py is unchanged and its result stands
_preregistration.H1_prime: models that RAISE phi under p1 have LOWER copy_score than models that FALL -- the direction observed at K=64, POST-HOC IN ORIGIN and PRE-REGISTERED IN TEST, on fresh probes rather than on the measurements that suggested it
_preregistration.why_direction_registered: F167's kill conditions were direction-agnostic (registry R10): a separation either way would have satisfied K2 while the hypothesis specified a sign. Registered here so that cannot recur.
_preregistration.noise_criterion: SE(gap) = sqrt(SE_hi^2 + SE_lo^2) with SE_m = sqrt(p(1-p)/N_m), N_m = K * n_seeds pooled probes; also the 2-point seed range as in F167; the LARGER is used. Conservative and not tunable after the fact.
_preregistration.kill_K1: ranges overlap -> the copy account is dropped
_preregistration.kill_K5: ranges separate but the gap does not exceed NOISE_FACTOR * SE(gap) -> NOT DECIDABLE FOR PRECISION again, and the remedy stays more probes, never a relaxed criterion
_preregistration.kill_direction: ranges separate with UP ABOVE DOWN -> H1' is refuted; that is the ORIGINAL H1's direction and would mean the K=64 sign was noise
_preregistration.order: boundary models first, so a truncated run still decides the gap
refusals: no p-value: 8 models cannot fail a significance test informatively
no rank correlation: below this project's ten-cluster floor (F149)

verdict: K=256 x 2 seeds = 512 probes per model, CPU float32. Falcon3-1B-Base 0.1777; SmolLM-1.7B 0.2324; Minerva-3B-base-v1.0 0.1250; Qwen1.5-1.8B 0.3535; pythia-410m 0.5098; pythia-410m-deduped 0.5508; llm-jp-3-1.8b 0.2227.  UP [0.1250, 0.1777], DOWN [0.2324, 0.5508].  NOT DECIDABLE FOR PRECISION again: gap 0.0547 against 2.0x noise 0.0598 (binomial 0.0252, seed 0.0299, larger used). Quadrupling the probes did not resolve it; the remedy stays more measurement. BOUNDARY: one arm (p1), 7 models, K=256, CPU float32, boundary models run first. No p-value and no rank correlation. The prior-art gate for induction heads and repetition self-reinforcement remains OWED and gates any write-up.

_analysis_provenance.note: sha256 of the analysis source at write time, plus the repo-local import closure. If any of these does not match the file on disk, the analysis was produced by a different version of the code -- re-run it before reading the numbers (issue #38; the imports half closes the same hole one level down the import graph). Third-party package versions are NOT covered.

_not_measured.why: cost. float32 CPU on a 16GB machine; these were the expensive cells and the gap is decided by the BOUNDARY models -- max(UP) and min(DOWN) -- which were run first.
_not_measured.can_they_move_the_boundary: no. Each unmeasured model scored >= 0.59 at K=64 (F167), and min(DOWN) here is 0.2324; moving the boundary would need a true score ~0.36 lower than its K=64 estimate, against a K=256 binomial SE of ~0.022. Stated as a bound, not as a guess: if any of them DID fall inside [0.1777, 0.2324] the verdict changes.

balance.gate_reason: p1 direction is usable: {'up': 2, 'down': 4}, minority class 2 >= 2. Chance is the majority-class rate 67%; report balanced accuracy against it, not raw agreement.

noise_estimator_reliability.what: seed_half_range / SE_binomial per model, against its distribution under PURE count noise. If the observed ratios sit inside the simulated spread, the across-seed term carries no information the binomial term lacks -- it is just a noisier estimate of the same thing, and the max() rule is then gated by estimator scatter.
noise_estimator_reliability.reading: a two-point range has sd ~0.6x its own mean, so across 7 models the largest ratio is expected to be roughly double the typical one BY CONSTRUCTION. More probes shrink the binomial term and the true seed variance but cannot stabilise a two-point ESTIMATOR of that variance; more SEEDS, or a paired design scoring the compared models on the SAME probe pairs, is the axis that would.
